notes:
- Comment on a message: A direct message is an activity, and AniList gives it replies like any other one - so the inbox row and the open message both carry a Comments button that opens the same thread the Activity feed uses, with liking, quoting, editing and deleting. Reading a conversation and talking about it no longer means leaving the app. The windowed read that chat view actually uses was still missing the message member, which is why a thread opened on a DM came back empty.
- Comments reach their oldest page: Older stopped one page short: the step back was asked twice, so the first 25 comments of any thread longer than 50 were unreachable while the row above the list kept promising them.
- A failed refresh retries the refresh: A background check that did not arrive shared its error field with a missing Older page, so the banner's Retry walked the thread backwards instead of fetching the comments that had not come.
- A like leaves the comment alone: Tapping a heart wrote back the whole comment as it was before the tap. If the thread refreshed while that request was out, the older text and count came back over the newer ones. A like now changes only the heart.
- Posting keeps your place in a thread: Posting into a thread you had scrolled up in revealed every comment the app had fetched. The window grows by the one comment that arrived now, which is yours.
- GIF tiles stop decoding originals: The picker treated any sample ending in .gif as a thumbnail. Measured against a live page, fifteen of twenty posts answer the sample URL equal to the file URL with no smaller copy at all - so up to twenty-four full-resolution animations, some 5200x5200, decoded into one grid. A sample now counts as a sample only when it is a different file and its own dimensions fit; otherwise the tile is the site's thumbnail still, and the comment still embeds the full animation.
- Recent GIFs draw as thumbnails, and update live: The recent-picks strip rebuilt each tile from the embed URL, which threw the tile budget away and left the strip stale until something else redrew the screen. It keeps the picked result now, and shows it the moment you pick it.
- Six reactions above an empty GIF search: The picker offers laughing, crying, angry, surprised, confused and blush before you type. Each was checked against the live index for animated results at the safe rating rather than guessed - smiling and wave return nothing there, and a chip that searches into an empty grid reads as a broken app.
- Photo uploads reach the host, and explain themselves: catbox answers over both address families behind its CDN, and on a connection with broken IPv6 the app gave up at the first failed route while a working address was in the list. When a browser-check page intercepts the request instead, the composer now says what it knows rather than showing you a line of HTML.
- Swiping the navigation bar no longer opens your inbox: Holding the bar and shoving it sideways moved less than one destination, and the bar asked did it move by whether the highlighted tab had changed - so a short drag counted as a still hold and fired the hold shortcut, which is the jump to Messages. Travel decides it now, a swipe that comes back asks for nothing, and the bar's own ring stops leaking touches to whatever it floats over.
- Animated bio images actually animate: A bio that embeds an image is no longer collapsed behind Show more: a collapsed bio is drawn as plain text, which has nowhere to put a picture, so the banner GIF a bio was built around appeared as the word Image. An image written inside a link renders as the picture and stays tappable, a bare .svg banner line is an image like the tagged form always was, and a dead embed finally looks dead instead of slow.
- Comments and GIF tiles move rather than jump: A comment that lands, an Older page arriving, a delete and a new page of results all re-laid the list out in one frame. They slide into place now, on the same springs the library grid uses.
- The text-size preview follows your finger: The sample animated toward a value that changed on every tick of the slider, so it lagged the thumb it was supposed to be following and never settled mid-drag.
- A spoiler can hold a picture: Hiding a reveal behind ~!...!~ showed the reader the words "Image" or a line of img(url) once they opened it: a spoiler drew its payload as styled text, and text has nowhere to put a picture. The payload is re-parsed now, so the thing people actually spoil - a colour, a character shot, a final frame - appears. A spoiler of words is untouched.
- The GIF picker decides how the embed sits: Alongside the width, a picked GIF can now go in normally, centred across the thread, or behind a spoiler's lid - the three framings AniList's own editor writes, so the preview is what other readers will see rather than markup they have to decode.
